findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present within the facility during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed chocolate sauces hot holding at 120F. Discussed with PIC, sauces were removed and reheated to 165F and returned to warmer. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed in house slushy mix to be missing date marking.  Discussed with PIC, education on date marking was provided and dates were added to items. Ensure any TCS item is properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed prep coolers to be missing thermometers. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and thermometers were brought to coolers. Ensure a thermometer is available in coolers.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed flies to be present throughout facility. Discussed with PIC, follow-up has been issued for 7/24/26. Ensure facility is pest free.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mops to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and mop was moved to mop ringer. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed multiple clothing items to be hanging on shelves. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were moved to an approved location. Ensure personal items are stored out of contact with food items.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice scoop handle to be in contact with ice at drive thru window. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was removed and placed in a way that handle is not in contact with ice. Ensure ice scoop handle is not in contact with ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed confetti cake toppings to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, item was pulled and disposed of. Ensure staff is monitoring date marking and is posing of any TCS food held longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is monitoring caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no Certified Food Manager to present upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, Certified Food Manager arrived during inspection, ensure there is a Certified Food Manager present at all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. The coving at the entrance to get behind the counter/into the kitchen is coming away. Replace it back onto the wall.
2. The mop sink is not attached with caulking to the wall. Ensure the mop sink is caulked.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Repair by next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop to be resting in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mop was removed and hanged in mop wringer. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents further contamination. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the kitchen hand sinks. Inspector asked PIC to put paper towels in the dispenser. Discussed with PIC. Ensure paper towels are replaced when they run out. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed a significant amount of milk splash and food debris within the base of the bottom reach-in cooler (above the ice cream toppings prep station). Discussed with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning of this cooler due to heighten use. Inspector asked PIC to have staff clean during the inspection. Inspector witnessed the wash, rinse, sanitize process. COS.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

(REPEAT) Observed the single-use spoons at the front cashier area and the drive thru to both have spoons going in either direction. Cease practice. Single-use utensils should be placed in one unison direction to avoid bare hand contact with food- and lip-contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. PIC instructed staff to don single-use gloves and correct the spoons. Ensure staff is aware to keep spoons in one order. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/15/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following areas in need of cleaning:
1. Interior of fryers - grease splash and debris within and on the doors.
2. Ceiling tiles and light covers above the ice cream topping prep table and directly behind it on the ceiling - food splash.
3. Walk-in freezer - debris under the shelving units.
4. Fan is blowing in the direction of the 3 compartment sink (on top of a shelving unit) - significantly dusty - clean the fan.

Discussed the above areas with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean these areas. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. The coving at the entrance to get behind the counter/into the kitchen is coming away. Replace it back onto the wall.
2. The mop sink is not attached with caulking to the wall. Ensure the mop sink is caulked.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Repair by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

A food handler was observed to moved from dish washing to the prep line. Gloves were donned without hand washing and RTE foods handled. PIC was instructed to review and enforce hand washing with staff to ensure proper procedures are taking place. The food handler in question was educated during th inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzles for both of the fountain drink machines are observed with an accumulation of bacterial slime. PIC stated that it was difficult to remove the inner part for cleaning and he believes that staff are only cleaning the back side of the items due to this. The nozzles were washed, rinsed and sanitized during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

1) Single service spoons in the drive through area are stored in a soiled container. The container was cleaned and the spoons replaced to correct. 2) Two wire mesh containers with single service spoons stored in them are observed with chocolate and Carmel splash on the inside of the containers. The containers were moved to wash and the spoons replaced to correct. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Spoons in the drive thru area are observed with the lip/food contact ends intermixed with the handles. The container was being cleaned as well and the new spoons placed into the container so that the food contact ends all faced the same direction.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival, PIC was not able to produce reporting agreements or other verification in relation to employees knowing about reportable symptoms or illness. A blank copy of the sheet given out by this department in relation to this was found in the managerial folder by the desk in the back. PIC made multiple copies and had present staff read and sign during the inspection to correct and PIC will have the remaining staff sign as they come in to work. Inspector suggested that the sheet be added to the hiring packet to ensure compliance with this section of the code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Cleaned and sanitized nozzles for the fountain machine were observed being re-attached to the drink machine with bare hands without hand washing prior to use. Inspector told the PIC that the employee should have washed their hands prior to handling food contact surfaces. The items were rewashed and attached properly. PIC also discussed with the employee while inspector continued the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzles for the fountain drink machine are observed with an accumulation of bacterial slime. PIC stated that the current practice is to wash every other day. Inspector suggested returning to every day and making sure that the nozzles are taken apart and scrubbed adequately so as to ensure any build ups are removed prior to sanitizing. The nozzles were washed, rinsed and sanitized during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) 

The sani buckets at the facility are observed with concentrations lower than required by the label (200 ppm) on the inspectors test strips. Per the PIC, the current policy is to change the buckets every 2 hours, and the most recent change was stated to be 20 minutes ago. Observations insinuate concentrations of approximately 100 ppm. The buckets were remade during the inspection and observed at 200 ppm from the machine.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) (REPEAT) Fruit/ drain flies are observed: 1) in the area behind the fountain drink at the counter, 2) by the mop sink in the back, 3) in the men's bathroom. Discussed with the PIC. They stated that Sentinel has been to the facility and sprayed. A compound has been placed down the mop sink drain twice and bleach is placed down it nightly. PIC is instructed to consult Sentinel again and to strive to remove the flies from the facility. Follow up is set for December 3, 2019.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Four items from the pre-opening are still in violation: 1) The plumbing clean out is not securely attached to the floor in front of the hand sink. 2)The grouting by the trash is in need of repair. 3) The wall needs o be sealed around the AC unit in the eastern wall. 4) The board at the bottom of the cashier's side of the counter needs to be securely attached/ replaced so that it provides a smooth easily clean able surface. PIC is instructed to repair these items prior to the next routine inspection.
